text: The Patriots' dominant 20-3 victory over the Steelers on Sunday was a study in defensive excellence and cautious offensive progress, though the win came with a significant injury price: film review revealed the defense thrived in man coverage schemes against Pittsburgh, while Drake Maye's performance offered both promise and areas for growth as he continues to develop the balance between patience and aggression that New England's system demands. TreVeyon Henderson found the end zone to spark an offense that, by most accounts, still hasn't quite recaptured the rhythm of last season's Super Bowl run, but the Patriots' defense did more than enough to carry the day and help the franchise become the first of the original AFL teams to reach 600 wins. The celebration was tempered, however, by the injury to starting right guard Mike Onwenu, whose initial X-rays confirmed a broken right ankle that will force the Patriots to shuffle their offensive line going forward. Head Coach Mike Vrabel addressed the win and the mounting injury concerns in his postgame press conference, offering perspective on what the film showed and what lies ahead for a team still seeking full offensive synchronization.
